mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary of the shareholder's country of origin or Luxembourg notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized passport copies and proof of residential address of each beneficial owner and proposed manager

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, managers, directors and authorized signatories against the UN Consolidated Sanctions List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List and Luxembourg national freeze lists; mandatory identification and enhanced due diligence for Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) including source-of-wealth verification per CSSF Regulation No 12-02; continuous transaction monitoring and re-screening at least annually and upon any triggering event.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS); official online portal: www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must include the legal-form suffix 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or the abbreviation 'SARL'. The name may be in French, German or any language using Latin characters, must be readily distinguishable from existing registered names and must not mislead the public. Non-Latin script names (e.g., Han characters, Cyrillic, Arabic) must be transliterated into Latin characters for RCS registration and must correspond to the phonetic representation adopted in the notarial deed.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Chambre de Commerce / Chamber of Commerce
Luxembourg (when used as a standalone token)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Reserve the chosen name via the LBR online portal; the reservation is protected for an initial validity period confirmed by LBR (ordinarily 30 days). Where the notarial incorporation deed cannot be executed before expiry, an administrative extension must be applied for prior to expiry, subject to the applicable LBR fee. Upon a name rejection, the applicant may resubmit an amended name electronically, retaining priority as of the original filing date where possible, or submit a reasoned administrative objection to the Minister of Justice within 30 days of the refusal notification. Final recourse lies with the Administrative Tribunal (Tribunal administratif) under the Law of 7 November 1996. The drafting notary coordinates all procedural steps.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A physical registered office (siège social) in Luxembourg is mandatory and must not be a mere letterbox address. A virtual-office administrative arrangement is tolerated only where the company demonstrates genuine operational substance in Luxembourg, including leased premises, local management, payroll and local accounting records. For an ISIC 5610 franchise-licensing and syrups supply-chain company, a purely virtual office is assessed as inadequate and materially increases substance-challenge risk; a physical office is strongly recommended.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified estimate: approximately 25% probability of an unannounced physical inspection within the first 24 months of operation for a low-risk standard franchise entity; the probability exceeds 50% where the entity claims treaty benefits or moves significant intercompany royalty and supply-chain revenue without commensurate local substance.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (as amended, incl. amendments of 2016 and 2021) — Articles 1, 12, 20, 26, 40, 44, 46 and 51; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 23 September 2021 on the RBE (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés — RCS), managed by the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) under the Ministry of Justice; insolvency-related publication to the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarised articles of incorporation (acte constitutif) for a Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL), followed by registration with the RCS and publication in the RESA.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital of EUR 12,000 (approx. USD 13,200) for a SARL; capital must be fully subscribed and, unless set out otherwise in the articles, paid up in cash prior to incorporation and evidenced by the notary; the capital is not held in escrow but must be placed at the disposal of the company and can be released for corporate expenses only after registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: First board resolution of Lu_SARL, adopted on the date of incorporation by unanimous consent of the founding shareholders: (1) confirming the subscription of each founder to the issued share capital as set forth in the articles of association; (2) adopting the registered office at the address stated in the articles of association and authorising the filing of the registration dossier with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register; (3) appointing the manager(s) and, where applicable, the members of the board of managers without remuneration for the first fiscal year; (4) authorising the secretary to execute all formalities, including electronic filing, publication, and registration with the RBE.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Legal due diligence and pre-incorporation checks
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / RCS online portal; notary public in the district of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct a Luxembourg notary to prepare the draft articles of association. Perform a company name search through the RCS online platform and LBR's name reservation system to ensure no identical registered name. Verify the identity of all founding shareholders and the beneficial owner information required under the RBE Act. Where a shareholder is a corporate entity, provide legal existence certificate and resolution of the corporate body authorising the subscription.
required_dossiers: Fully completed incorporation questionnaire
Proposed articles of association (draft, in French/German/English with notary translation)
Name reservation certificate (if obtained)
Passport or ID copies and proof of residential address for each founder and manager
Foreign corporate shareholder: certificate of incorporation, excerpt from register, board resolution authorising the subscription
Bank certificate evidencing payment of the minimum share capital (or notary trust account confirmation)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or queried, submit a new name request through the LBR portal or appeal to the RCS registration office; any queries regarding documents are communicated by the notary and must be cured within 15 days, failing which the file is closed without prejudice to a fresh filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and notarisation of the articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (notaire) competent in the district of the registered office; RCS to receive the notarial deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Arrange a notarial appointment for the execution of the deed of incorporation. All founders must appear in person or by proxy before the notary. The notary verifies the payment of the share capital, the lawfulness of the corporate purpose, and the capacity of the parties, then authenticates the deed. The notary triggers the immediate electronic transmission of the deed to the RCS for registration and to the RESA for publication.
required_dossiers: Final draft articles of association approved by all founders
Original bank proof of payment of share capital
List of subscribing shareholders with number and value of shares
Certified identity documents of signatories
Proxy forms if representation used
Declaration of absence of professional interdiction/bankruptcy for the manager(s)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Should the notary identify any irregularity (e.g., unpaid capital or missing manager declaration), the deed is not executed until the defect is cured. If the RCS rejects the filing, the notary modifies the deed by unilateral rectification deed or requires a supplementary deed; curative filings are processed under the same SLA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCS – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary files the deed of incorporation, together with the standard registration form, electronically via the LBR portal. The RCS verifies the compliance of the articles with the Law of 1915 and the identity of the signatories, then issues the RCS registration certificate (extrait) showing the company number (e.g., B 000000). The notification is published in the RESA within one business day. The RBE filing is submitted by the notary simultaneously for the official beneficial owners.
required_dossiers: Authenticated deed of incorporation from the notary
RCS filing form (formulaire de dépôt)
Proof of registered office address (lease or business licence for real estate if needed)
RBE declaration with beneficial owner details
Statement by the manager accepting his functions
Certified true copies of banking confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS questions the corporate object or the legal form, the applicant via the notary submits supplementary clarifications or amends the articles by a private deed of amendment signed before the notary. RCS objections must be cured within one month to avoid cancellation ex officio.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA) and effective legal existence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RESA publication service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following RCS registration, the LBR publishes the mandatory extract of the deed (name, legal form, registered office, share capital, managers) in the RESA. The extract is transmitted automatically by the RCS; no separate applicant action is required. The publication grants third-party effectiveness of the incorporation. Confirm the publication by downloading the RESA excerpt from the LBR website.
required_dossiers: RCS registration number and extract (generated automatically)
No additional applicant documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RESA publication contains clerical errors, provide the notary with a written request for rectification; the notary files a supplementary deed with the RCS and the LBR corrects the electronic publication within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration formalities, RBE filing and corporate seal, opening of bank account, social security registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: LBR (RBE); Luxembourg tax administration (AEDT, registration duty office); Social Security Centre (Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale – CCSS); commercial bank in Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, the notary confirms the RBE filing; the company files the final RBE declaration directly online if changes occur within 30 days. Apply at the AEDT for the business incorporation tax number (numéro de TVA) and for the EIN number for corporate tax. Register the company with the CCSS as an employer if hiring personnel. Order the corporate seal (cachet social) and open a corporate bank account for ongoing operations, presenting the RCS extract and corporate documents.
required_dossiers: RCS certificate of registration
RESA publication excerpt
Final RBE declaration (or notary confirmation)
Articles of association and powers of attorney for the manager
Manager's residence permit / Luxembourg ID where applicable
Lease contract of registered office
Bank account opening forms and KYC (structure chart, beneficial owner declarations)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office delays issuance of the VAT number, file a reminder letter via the dedicated e-offices portal; if the CCSS rejects the registration, cure any missing social security number of the manager and re-submit within 10 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Commune of the place of establishment – Service de l'aménagement urbain / Département des licences d'exploitation; under the Ministry of the Economy and the Ministry of Health for food-related operational permits.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licence d'établissement (business establishment licence) for a beverage preparation and franchise operations activity under the Law of 2 September 2011 on access to the professions of artisan, merchant, industrialist and liberal activity; alternatively a commercial/industrial licence issued by the Ministry of the Economy for franchise licensing activities, and an authorisation under the Food Safety Act for the preparation and distribution of bubble tea products.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Luxembourg Administration de l'Environnement (Environmental Protection Agency) – Ministère de l'Environnement, du Climat et du Dévelement durable; urban planning service of the local commune.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category: Registration / Notice — Class 2 under the Annex of the Law of 10 June 1999 on the management of integrated environmental protection for light food and beverage production units with limited wastewater discharges; not exceeding the thresholds requiring a Full EIA Report unless the franchise facility includes industrial-scale syrup production with solvent/storage capacities above Class 2 thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: compliance with the drainage regulation of the local commune and the Luxembourg Law of 19 December 2008 on water management — total suspended solids (MO) < 60 mg/l and COD < 150 mg/l for process water discharges to municipal sewer; NO direct discharge to groundwater without pre-treatment; VOC: compliance with the VOC emissions regulation of 2004 (Grand-Ducal Regulation of 21 November 2003) for potential solvent emissions from cleaning agents; waste handling: proper sorting and disposal under the Law of 21 March 2012 on waste management, with tracking documents for cooking oils (food waste) and recycling of packaging.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification: obtain an attestation from the communal fire department (Service d'incendie et de secours) based on the installation of extinguishing equipment and emergency exits; for premises open to the public obtain the certificate of compliance with fire safety regulations from the local commune. Structural load inspections: where the premises hosts industrial syrups tanks or franchised tea equipment, provide a structural load report certified by a Luxembourg engineer stating the floor load capacity. Workplace clearance: obtain an occupational health and safety clearance from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) confirming compliance with the Labour Code, including an adequate ventilation system, mechanical/electrical safety for beverage machines, and ergonomic workstations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Luxembourg Inland Revenue (Administration des contributions directes, ACD) for direct taxes; Registration, Estates and VAT Authority (Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA, AEDT) for VAT. Central e-portal: MyGuichet.lu (https://guichet.public.lu).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities must: (1) incorporate through the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) and obtain an RCS registration number; (2) obtain a national identification number (matricule) from the Social Security Centre or its delegated registrar; (3) apply to the AEDT for a Luxembourg VAT number (numéro de TVA intracommunautaire) by filing standard VAT registration form 640 via MyGuichet.lu, enclosing articles of incorporation, RCS excerpt, identity documents, and a Luxembourg tax representative appointment if not EU-established; (4) register for corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités), municipal business tax, and net wealth tax with the competent ACD office at the registered office; (5) optionally request an advance tax ruling (article 29a LIR) for complex international arrangements.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; a Luxembourg SARL is a resident company fully taxable on worldwide income (corporate income tax, municipal business tax, net wealth tax) with no general pass-through to shareholders; shareholders, however, enjoy the participation exemption under certain conditions.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists. Available statutory mechanisms: (1) election of the Luxembourg participation exemption regime (Article 166 LIR) for qualifying dividends and capital gains; (2) fiscal unity / tax consolidation election (intégration fiscale) for 95%-or-more-held resident subsidiaries, subject to ACD approval; (3) election for VAT grouping (assujetti unique) between Luxembourg-established related persons; (4) election of the reduced VAT flat-rate margin scheme, where applicable; (5) filing of an advance tax ruling application with the ACD; (6) depreciation and loss-carry-forward elections in accordance with standard Luxembourg GAAP and LIR rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value Added Tax, TVA) under the Luxembourg VAT Act (Loi TVA), transposing EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual turnover threshold for the small business exemption (Article 57 Loi TVA); mandatory VAT registration from the first euro for non-established taxable persons, reverse-charge transactions, intra-Community acquisitions, and supplies of distance sales goods where applicable.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, government API stamping, or digital seal regime. Luxembourg has adopted a phased mandatory B2B e-invoicing regime: Luxembourg-established suppliers must issue structured e-invoices (PEPPOL BIS 3.0 / EN 16931 compliant) for domestic B2B supplies from 1 February 2026 under the law of 20 July 2024; transmission uses PEPPOL access points without central government clearance; B2G e-invoicing via e-procurement is already mandatory. VAT returns (form 1005), EC Sales Lists, and recapitulative statements remain periodical.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Articles 56 and 58 Loi TVA, 0% VAT applies to: (1) supplies of goods physically dispatched or transported outside Luxembourg and outside the EU, evidenced by customs export documentation; (2) intra-Community (EU) supplies where the customer's valid EU VAT number is confirmed through VIES and the EC Sales List is filed; (3) services directly related to export goods (e.g., transport, handling, inspection); and (4) royalties, franchise fees, and offshore services rendered to a non-EU customer established outside the EU, provided the place of supply is outside the EU under the B2B receipt rule (Article 46 Loi TVA) and economic substance/beneficial use is documented in the underlying franchise and licence agreements.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (AES electronic record / Single Administrative Document accompanying exportation)
Commercial invoice and export invoice issued by the Luxembourg SARL
Transport proof: Bill of Lading (sea), CMR (road), AWB (air), with packing list
Customer delivery confirmation or signed proof of delivery
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT bank receipt evidencing foreign-exchange payment of the invoice
Franchise, licence, or royalty agreement documenting foreign place of use, customer establishment, and economic substance
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg VAT audits apply a strict evidentiary standard. Export zero-rating claimed without complete export documentation is recharacterized at the 17% standard rate, with late-interest of 0.6% per month and penalties of up to 10% of the tax for good-faith errors, 100% plus criminal fines for fraudulent claims (Article 188 Loi TVA). VAT refunds already received may be retroactively clawed back within the standard five-year assessment window; no limitation period applies in fraud cases, and penalties may extend to corporate representatives. Substantiation bundles must be retained for at least six years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) as national central bank within the Eurosystem; European Central Bank (ECB) sets monetary policy and foreign-exchange operations for the euro; Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) as prudential and conduct supervisor for all Luxembourg credit institutions, payment institutions, and e-money institutions; Ministère des Finances as legislative steward of financial-sector law
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg operates a fully liberalised euro-area capital and current account regime under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) and Council Directive 88/361/EEC. The euro is freely convertible, and no exchange-control authorisation, central-bank approval, or ministry permit is required for inward FDI, equity injections, shareholder loans, dividend distributions, royalty remittances, trade payments, or franchise-fee repatriation to EU or non-EU counterparties. Profit remittance is commercially unrestricted but taxed at the source: Luxembourg corporate income tax (17% base CIT plus 7% solidarity surcharge) and municipal business tax (6.75% at Luxembourg City) produce a combined CIT burden of approximately 24.94%; dividend distributions to shareholders attract a 15% domestic withholding tax, reducible under tax treaties. Substance requirements under the Luxembourg CIR administrative circular of 31 May 2019 (and CSSF AML supervision) apply. The only genuine hurdles are (i) screening against EU financial sanctions and CSSF/Ministère des Affaires Étrangères lists, (ii) cash-movement declaration obligations for cross-border transfers of cash exceeding €10,000 under Regulation (EU) 2018/1672, and (iii) demonstration of economic substance at the SARL level to validate the treasury and franchise licensing model.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Neither Luxembourg domestic law, BCL regulations, CSSF guidance, nor Eurosystem rules impose any statutory timeline, mandatory conversion ratio to euro, repatriation window, or surrender obligation for export receipts of goods (bubble-tea syrups, concentrates, packaging) or services (franchise licensing fees, royalties, management fees). Export proceeds and franchise income may be retained indefinitely in EUR or any foreign currency, held in foreign-currency accounts with authorised Luxembourg credit institutions, or applied directly to import and treasury obligations. Only standard AML record-keeping thresholds, sanctions screening, and the SARL's CRS/FATCA reporting obligations apply.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account and Trade Finance / LC Desk
Wealth/Private Banking Account (not recommended as primary treasury)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: MEDIUM as secondary operating rail; LOW as sole or primary treasury rail. A Luxembourg-resident SARL may lawfully open accounts with Luxembourg CSSF-authorised payment institutions and e-money institutions under PSD2, and with EU-licensed EMIs exercising the passporting regime. However, offshore digital EMIs (FCA-authorised UK EMIs, Lithuanian, Estonian, or Dutch digital banks) are not credit institutions: they cannot issue or confirm commercial letters of credit, generally lack direct correspondent-bank access to all corridors (notably China/US), do not support SWIFT MT202 COV or documentary collections in all jurisdictions, and carry concentration and resolution risk. UK EMIs additionally lost EU passporting post-Brexit. For a franchise and goods-supply treasury, the EMI channel is acceptable only for local franchisee collection (local POS, e-commerce checkout, small-value royalty aggregation) under a merchant-acquiring agreement, with daily automated concentration (T+1) to the tier-1 Luxembourg bank. All funds above a de-minimis threshold (€10,000 per flow) must settle through a full-service credit institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of at least one director or authorised signatory (and in practice the ultimate beneficial owner(s) above 10%) at the Luxembourg bank premises is the de facto industry standard for opening a corporate account for a non-resident-owned SARL. Remote onboarding using video-identification integrated with an eIDAS qualified electronic signature is technically permissible for EU/EEA beneficial owners. For non-EU owners (APAC and China franchise network), Luxembourg tier-1 banks require: (i) an in-person interview at the head office or branch, or (ii) a remotely conducted live video KYC interview with the compliance officer, supplemented by verified qualification of the ID documents (apostille or consular legalisation), full notarised translation into French/German/English, and a board resolution granting specific account-opening authority. Practical mandate: one physical visit by a director holding a general power of attorney, or appointment of a Luxembourg corporate-services provider as registered and authorised agent for onboarding; the CSSF AML circular (Loi du 12 novembre 2004, CSSF Regulation 12-02) obliges the bank to identify every signatory and UBO under a risk-based approach; a purely non-face-to-face opening for a cross-border franchise treasury is unlikely to be accepted except with a substantial account history and an existing banking relationship.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Multi-jurisdictional franchise architecture with intermediate holding vehicles and opaque beneficial-ownership layers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full Luxembourg RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) filing confirmation; signed organisational-group chart; LEI for the SARL and parent entities; notarised shareholder register; 12-month bank statements of immediate shareholder and intermediate vehicles; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence for all UBOs; proof of tax residence certificates for every legal-entity shareholder; explanation of commercial rationale for each layer; if any layer is in a non-cooperative jurisdiction, a legal opinion from counsel in that jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border royalty flows to/from Asian franchisees and high-frequency related-party trade in syrups, presenting transfer-pricing or round-tripping suspicion
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master franchise agreements and sub-franchise chain documentation; IP registration certificates (Benelux trademarks, international trademark registrations under Madrid Protocol); royalty-calculation spreadsheet and invoice trail (with franchisee sales reports); supply-chain transportation documents (B/L, AWB, CMR, customs declarations, commercial invoices, packing lists); transfer-pricing policy with OECD-compliant comparability analysis and Luxembourg local-file documentation; UBO and sanctions/PEP screening reports for each franchisee; VAT and customs records evidencing physical (rather than phantom) trade flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual transaction velocity relative to declared minimum capital and short corporate history (newly incorporated SARL with immediate large cross-border flows)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 12-month treasury forecast and cash-flow model approved by the board; board minutes authorising transaction templates and counterparty limits; statutory audit or reviewed financial statements; evidence of actual substance (lease agreement, payroll records, office photos, social-security and direct-tax filings); bank reference letters from an existing institution; explanation of the seasonal working-capital cycle of syrup procurement and franchise royalty collections.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of shareholder loans instead of fully paid equity (thin-capitalisation or disguised-dividend suspicion by the compliance and tax departments)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed shareholder loan agreement with at-arm's-length interest rate and maturity; board resolutions approving the loan; proof of actual disbursement and repayment flows; debt-equity ratio memorandum prepared by a Luxembourg tax advisor; advance pricing agreement or advance tax ruling (demande de rescrit) if pursued; explanation of commercial rationale for debt funding (flexible repatriation, group cash pooling); audited accounts showing the liability position and interest accruals.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Franchise royalty collection through multiple POS/acquirer channels causing fragmentation and potential commingling of consumer funds
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Merchant-acquirer agreements with all PSPs; PCI-DSS attestation of compliance; settlement-flow maps showing daily sweep to the Luxembourg operating account; treasury policy requiring no commingling of franchisee consumer proceeds with company-operational funds; reconciliation trail between POS reports, acquirer settlements and ledger entries; escalation procedures for unexplained credits; independent IT auditor's report on payment-flow segregation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity or shareholder-loan capital is injected via SWIFT MT103 from the parent/shareholder account to the SARL's EUR operating account at a tier-1 Luxembourg bank. Recommended Eurosystem/ECB Balance-of-Payments classification purpose codes: for equity injections use 'S.12 – Equity capital of direct investor in direct-investment enterprise' / BoP item 'A.5A1'; for shareholder loans use 'S.13 – Other capital of direct investor (loans)' / BoP item 'A.5B2' with supplementary trade-description 'shareholder loan'. In practice, banks map these to internal purpose fields; the remitter must state clearly: 'Equity contribution LU_SARL' or 'Shareholder loan to LU_SARL' with reference to the notarised/private subscription document. The mandatory verification bundle contains: (i) SARL board resolution authorising the issuance or loan drawdown; (ii) notarised contribution statement or private act with share-register update within one month; (iii) updated RBE filing if UBO percentages change; (iv) signed shareholder loan agreement with interest-rate clause; (v) source-of-funds evidence for any transfer ≥ EUR 15,000 and for any cross-border wire ranked higher risk (APAC corridor); (vi) LEI of the remitting entity; (vii) bank's standard AML questionnaire and negative-news declaration for the remitter. No CSSF or BCL prior authorisation is required for capital movement into Luxembourg; however, the bank may place funds on an 'awaiting-substance' hold until the corporate file is complete, and the capital injection must be booked under Luxembourg GAAP/IFRS capital-reserve rules.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails for the franchise treasury: (i) SWIFT MT103 (Single Customer Credit Transfer) for all direct supplier, vendor, and royalty-disbursement payments in EUR/USD/CNH; (ii) irrevocable Commercial Letters of Credit (including confirmed LCs where required) governed by UCP 600 and eUCP, for high-value syrup concentrate purchases from Asian bottling partners; (iii) SEPA Credit Transfer and SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst) for EU suppliers and franchisee rebates up to €100,000; (iv) SWIFT MT202/MT202 COV for interbank cover payments and treasury cash-concentration between the SARL's own accounts; and (v) PCI-DSS-compliant merchant acquiring / local-POS rails for franchisee store-level collection with T+1 sweep to the operating account. Outbound wires must state a precise purpose text referencing invoice/contract numbers (e.g., 'syrup import Beijing – invoice #'), carry full beneficiary legal name, address, IBAN-equivalent, and BIC/SWIFT, be screened against EU sanctions and PEP lists before submission, and comply with the bank's transaction-monitoring thresholds; payments above €10,000 in cash, and any suspicious pattern, trigger CSSF/FIU reporting. Trade payments via LC must be supported by compliant transport documents (B/L or AWB, commercial invoice, packing list, certificate of origin, quality certificates) matching the underlying contract, and the SARL must maintain an ISBP 745-compliant presentation pack.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/USD and EUR/CNH FX Forwards (tenors up to 12 months, onshore/offshore CNH deliverable)
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on EUR/CNY for the offshore official renminbi rate, settled in EUR
Cross-Currency Swaps (XCCY) aligning syrup-import payable currencies with franchise-royalty receivable currencies
European-style FX Options (plain-vanilla calls/puts) with upfront premium for strategic repricing cover
Foreign Exchange Swaps (FX swaps) for short-term liquidity bridging between the SARL's EUR, USD and CNH accounts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (financial statements) deposit and publication
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholder approval required within six months of financial year-end (calendar-year: by 30 June); deposit with RCS no later than one month after approval (calendar-year: by 31 July)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines of EUR 500 to 5,000 for late filing; closure of the registration file and liquidator appointment after continued default; public forced notice may be published in the LBR

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial owners (UBO register declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – UBO Register (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of the anniversary of the entity's RCS registration date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to EUR 5,000 (individuals: EUR 1,250–2,500; legal entities: EUR 5,000); criminal sanctions for intentional omission include imprisonment and fines up to EUR 25,000; RCS clearance is blocked for certain corporate acts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (déclaration de l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) and municipal business tax declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year taxpayers: due 30 June following the relevant fiscal year; professional extension normally available until 31 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest at 0.6% per month on overdue tax; ex officio assessment based on available information; late-filing and omission penalties up to EUR 25,000 under the General Tax Law

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual net wealth tax return (déclaration de l'impôt sur la fortune)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year taxpayers: due 30 June following the relevant fiscal year; professional extension normally available until 31 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest at 0.6% per month; late-filing penalties and ex officio assessment; additional surcharges of 5%–10% may apply to the wealth tax due

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT return (déclaration annuelle TVA) and EC sales listing (récapitulatif)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be filed by 1 May of the following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest of 0.8% per month; late-filing fines up to 5% of the VAT due; fixed penalties for non-filing (EUR 250 per return and per month of delay)

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent statutory audit is mandatory where more than one of the following three thresholds is exceeded on the balance-sheet date for two consecutive years: total balance sheet greater than EUR 4.4 million; net turnover greater than EUR 8.8 million; average workforce greater than 50 employees. Audit is also required for public-interest entities, parent undertakings of a qualifying group, and where the SARL is required to present consolidated accounts.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 19 December 2002 on commercial companies, trade registers and accounting (implementing Directive 2013/34/EU); EU-endorsed IFRS may be adopted for statutory accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL must confirm its beneficial owners annually with the UBO Register in the month following the anniversary of its RCS registration. Any share transfer after the confirmation date must be reflected in the next annual update; share transfers of more than 25% beneficial ownership require timely indication to the register.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (list of shares and shareholders)
Register of Minutes of Shareholders' Meetings
Register of financial statements and auditor reports

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 17% (Luxembourg corporate income tax for taxable income exceeding EUR 175,000; combined effective burden in Luxembourg City including the 7% employment fund solidarity surcharge and municipal business tax of 6.75% approximates 24.94%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holidays apply to an SARL. Preferential regimes: (1) IP Box under Art. 50bis LIR granting an 80% deduction on qualifying IP-derived income (franchise trademarks, boba tea recipes, know-how, syrup formulations) producing an effective rate near 5.04%; (2) participation exemption under Art. 166 LIR exempting 100% of qualifying dividends and realized capital gains where the SARL holds at least 10% or an acquisition cost of at least EUR 6 million for an uninterrupted 12-month period; (3) net wealth tax mitigation via the grandfathered participation exemption; losses are legally usable on an indefinite carry-forward basis under Art. 110 LIR.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 620 - Annual Luxembourg Corporate Income Tax, Municipal Business Tax and Net Wealth Tax Return (Déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités, l'impôt commercial communal et l'impôt sur la fortune); electronically lodged through the eCDF module on MyGuichet.lu using Luxtrust electronic identification; paper filing only with prior consent of the Administration des contributions directes (ACD).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual - a single consolidated return covering CIT, municipal business tax and net wealth tax for the completed fiscal year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return must be filed by 31 December of the calendar year following the fiscal year end (for a 31 December year-end, due date is 31 December of the following year); the ACD may grant an administrative extension to 31 March of the subsequent year only upon justified written request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, RCSL registration number, registered seat, legal form (SARL), exact address of effective management, and opening and closing dates of the fiscal year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders do not file this return individually; the SARL must disclose each shareholder's country of residence, shareholding percentage and ownership chain for treaty and ultimate beneficial owner coherence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Pre-tax commercial profit or loss determined from the audited annual accounts, including franchise royalties received, syrup and supply-chain revenues, and sub-licensing income attributable to the ISIC 5610 activity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident related-party payments appear only as deductible expenses of the SARL; a full intercompany transaction schedule and contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation must be annexed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Qualifying net income derived from intellectual property (boba tea brand, recipes, secret formulas, industrial know-how) after the 80% exemption; requires documentary proof of asset ownership, development chain and economic substance in Luxembourg.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The deduction is denied where the IP was merely acquired and licensed back to the non-resident franchisor in a circular back-to-back arrangement without local R&D or management substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: 100% exemption for dividend income and realized capital gains from qualifying subsidiaries held at 10% or more (or acquired for at least EUR 6 million) for a 12-month holding period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exemption is claimed at the level of the Luxembourg SARL; the non-resident parent does not file in Luxembourg and applies its own domestic and treaty treatment on distributions received.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of taxable net assets (immovable property, receivables, financial assets less debts) subject to the 0.5% annual net wealth tax; qualifying participation shareholdings may be excluded where the gross participation exemption conditions are met.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Assets of the non-resident shareholder are excluded from the SARL's net wealth; only assets legally owned by the Luxembourg entity are declared.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 60 - Tax adjustments and loss utilization
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back of non-deductible expenses and hidden distributions, application of arm's length transfer pricing adjustments, and chronological off-set of available prior-year losses against current assessable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss off-set operates only at Luxembourg level; losses of foreign permanent establishments cannot reduce the Luxembourg taxable base where the applicable treaty follows the exemption method.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or omitted filing triggers taxation d'office (estimated assessment), monthly late-payment interest of 0.6% on the assessed amount, a 10% droit en sus surcharge on the additional tax, a coercive daily fine of up to EUR 50 imposed by the tax director for continued non-filing, and separate administrative fines against the managing director; intentional concealment attracts criminal penalties under Article 174-176 of the General Tax Law.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Country-by-Country Report and CbC Filing Notification - lodged through the ACD's electronic CbC portal (eCDF module) for automatic exchange with all EU and treaty partner competent authorities.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual - filed within 12 months after the end of the group's reporting fiscal year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The Luxembourg ultimate parent entity files the CbC report within 12 months of the fiscal year end; secondary local filing may be imposed on the SARL where the non-resident ultimate parent has not filed a qualifying CbC report in its own jurisdiction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Revenue from unrelated and related parties, profit or loss before income tax, income tax paid and accrued, stated capital, accumulated earnings, number of employees, and tangible assets allocated to each jurisdiction of the franchise group.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Luxembourg SARL is reported as a Luxembourg constituent entity; royalty and syrup supply-chain flows with the non-resident parent are allocated to Luxembourg in line with arm's length accounting.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification of each group entity by legal residence, including the LU SARL (RCSL number), with the main business activity classified as franchise licensing, IP holding and syrup supply chain.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident franchisees are listed by residence country; confirmation of the absence of permanent establishments of the SARL abroad must be supported by treaty analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Narrative on data sources and intercompany pricing policies covering the franchise royalty rate, syrup resale mark-up and allocation of IP income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Describe the arm's length methodology applied to cross-border payments and any adjustments agreed with foreign tax administrations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file the CbC report or notification exposes the SARL and its managers to a fine of up to EUR 250,000, per-entity documentation penalties, estimated reassessment of taxable profits and the full 10% surcharge plus 0.6% monthly interest; aggravating circumstances may attract criminal prosecution for tax evasion.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% withholding tax on Luxembourg-source dividends under Article 147 LIR; fully reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (2011/96/EU) where the foreign parent company holds at least 10% of the Luxembourg SARL for 12 uninterrupted months; bilateral double taxation agreements reduce the rate to 0-15% for treaty-protected shareholders.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Relief at source requires the non-resident shareholder to deliver a valid Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) issued by its home tax authority and the completed treaty benefit statement to the Luxembourg paying SARL before the distribution date; the ACD may be asked to confirm the reduced rate under the advance treaty relief procedure. Where withholding was applied at 15%, the shareholder may file a refund claim with the ACD within five years. Under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive, the SARL applies the 0% rate upon receipt of the parent's residence certificate and written confirmation of the 10% and 12-month holding conditions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg imposes no general withholding tax on arm's length royalties or interest paid to non-residents; the EU Interest and Royalties Directive (2003/49/EC) secures a 0% rate for related EU companies holding at least 25% for 24 months; a 20% final withholding tax applies to interest and royalty payments made to related entities resident in jurisdictions listed on the EU list of non-cooperative tax jurisdictions (effective for payments from 1 January 2021); treaty rates typically range between 0% and 15% for royalties and 0% and 10% for interest.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 750,000,000 consolidated group revenue - the statutory threshold for mandatory Master File, Local File and Country-by-Country reporting under EU Directive 2016/881 as implemented in Luxembourg. Below this threshold the SARL must nevertheless maintain contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation for franchise royalty, syrup supply and IP licensing transactions to withstand an ACD audit; the arm's length principle applies to all related-party transactions without any revenue-based exemption.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg applies the full OECD and EU anti-abuse acquis: (1) the domestic GAAR in Article 6 LIR authorizing the ACD to disregard transactions lacking valid economic substance; (2) the Principal Purpose Test (PPT) under the BEPS Multilateral Instrument embedded in Luxembourg's treaties denying treaty benefits to artificial conduit arrangements; (3) the 2023 Pillar Two law introducing a 15% global minimum effective tax rate for multinational groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million effective for fiscal years beginning on or after 31 December 2023; (4) the substance requirements of the ACD circulars (LIR 56/1 - 56/1bis) requiring genuine local management, qualified staff, proportionate equity, real offices and board decisions taken in Luxembourg for entities benefiting from the IP Box, participation exemption and treaty access. A letterbox franchise holding without these attributes is re-characterized as sham and stripped of all tax benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of franchise royalty income, syrup supply-chain turnover, or concealed financial accounts; filing a false Form 620 declaring fictitious expenses or routing boba tea franchise fees to offshore shell accounts without economic justification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administratively: taxation d'office with reassessment at the combined 24.94% effective rate, a 10% droit en sus surcharge and monthly late-payment interest of 0.6%; criminally: imprisonment of up to 5 years, fines of up to EUR 250,000 for clandestine tax evasion, and confiscation of assets linked to the evasion scheme.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The managing director who knowingly signs a false return faces personal criminal conviction, fines and imprisonment; the ACD may pierce the corporate veil where the SARL is a pure facade, imposing civil restitution on the director; courts may issue travel bans, seizure orders and professional disqualification during the criminal procedure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Sham Company, Shell Arrangement and Treaty Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Luxembourg SARL as a letterbox entity without staff, premises, bank accounts or local management decisions while routing global franchise royalty and syrup supply-chain profits into Luxembourg solely to exploit the treaty network and IP Box regime.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of all treaty benefits under the Principal Purpose Test; re-characterization of the structure under Article 6 LIR; assessment of hidden profits as constructive dividends subject to 15% withholding; back taxes at 24.94% with the 10% surcharge and 0.6% monthly interest; in extreme cases the ACD initiates judicial dissolution and de-registration of the entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid corporate tax where the letterbox operation constitutes a serious and characteristic breach of their statutory duties; courts apply the fictitiousness doctrine to disregard the SARL's separate personality and attach director assets; travel bans and imprisonment of up to 5 years apply for complicity in treaty fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation Failure and Profit Shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting a 0.5% royalty rate for the global boba tea brand while foreign operating subsidiaries retain no residual profit; pricing syrup supplies to related franchisees below cost; failure to prepare the Master File and Local File despite qualifying group revenue of EUR 750 million or more.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Upward adjustment of Luxembourg assessable income to the arm's length result; disallowance of undocumented intercompany payments; 10% droit en sus on the additional assessment; 0.6% monthly late interest; fines of up to EUR 250,000 for incomplete CbC, Master File or Local File obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve intragroup terms without economic analysis are civilly liable for the additional tax and interest; knowing participation in a profit-shifting scheme triggers criminal liability for tax evasion, personal fines, imprisonment and travel bans in cross-border EU joint investigation cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/CFT and Ultimate Beneficial Owner Registration Infractions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to identify and register the global franchise founder as the ultimate beneficial owner in the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE); omission of suspicious transaction reports to the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit; use of cash-heavy local syrup sales channels to obscure the ownership and source of funds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines of up to EUR 250,000 for UBO registration failures; the AML Law of 12 November 2004, as amended, imposes fines of up to EUR 5,000,000 or 10% of annual turnover for professional entities, withdrawal of the operating licence and confiscation orders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face criminal money laundering sanctions of imprisonment from 3 months to 5 years and fines up to EUR 1,250,000; confiscation of proceeds, judicial travel bans, temporary barring from corporate management and personal civil restitution to the tax and customs authorities are available against natural-person directors.
